newsitem.title: USA: L.A. Gear expects Q4 restructuring charge.
newsitem.headline: L.A. Gear expects Q4 restructuring charge.

text.p: L.A. Gear Inc said it expected a charge of between $28 million and $33 million on its operating results for the fourth quarter due to a restructuring plan to reduce costs.
The company said in a statement that it had adopted the plan in light of continuing operating losses.
"(It was) aimed at bringing the company's operating expenses in line with its anticipated sales base," the statement said.

The company said the restructuring plan consisted of an estimated 55-percent reduction in its full-time domestic workforce from about 310 to 140 employees. In addition it would reduce corporate overheads through space consolidation at the company's headquarters and distribution centre operations.
It also said the plan would consolidate and restructure its European operations.
It said it expected its fourth-quarter operating results would be adversely affected by between $28 million and $33 million of restructuring charges in connection with the implementation of the plan.

It is expected that about $17 million to $20 million of the estimated restructuring charge will be of a non-cash nature, primarily related to asset write-downs and goodwill write-offs associated with some of the company's European subsidiaries.

The company said domestic workforce reductions would occur in the first quarter of fiscal 1997, and substantially all of the estimated cash costs associated with the plan would be incurred over the next six to 12 months.
L.A. Gear earlier said that it anticipated a loss for the fourth quarter and year ended November 30, 1996.
